"Brandin Adar Knight was born Dec. 16, 1981 in Livingston, NJ...is the son of Mel and Brenda Knight.") is an American [[basketball]] coach and former player who is associate head coach for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights]]. == Early life == Knight grew up in [[East Orange, New Jersey]], and played high school ball at [[Seton Hall Preparatory School]] in [[West Orange, New Jersey]].{{cite news |author1=Jim Carty |title=Scouts haven't learned from Knight |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98088731/scouts-havent-learned-from-knight/ |access-date=21 March 2022 |work=[[The Central New Jersey Home News]] |date=11 July 1998 |page=C5}} He is the brother of [[Brevin Knight]].{{cite news |author1=Chris Iseman |title='He's ready to be a head coach': Rutgers assistant Brandin Knight helping lift Scarlet Knights |url=https://eu.app.com/story/sports/college/rutgers/2021/02/26/rutgers-nj-basketball-assistant-coach-brandin-knight/4546255001/ |access-date=18 March 2022 |work=[[Asbury Park Press]]}} == College career == A 6'0" [[point guard]], Knight played for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball]] team,{{cite news |author1=Craig Meyer |title=How Brandin Knight took Pitt basketball from afterthought to national power |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2020/10/20/pitt-panthers-basketball-brandin-knight-ben-howland-hall-of-fame-jamie-dixon-jaron-brown/stories/202010110038 |access-date=18 March 2022 |work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |date=20 October 2020}} where he scored 1,440 career points. He was one of ten players named to the 2002–03 Wooden [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] team and was [[Associated Press]] honorable mention All-American that same season. Knight was also selected as an Associated Press Third Team All-American and ''[[Sporting News]]'' Second Team All-American in 2002–02.{{Cite web |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/pitt/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/0809-mediaguide-section8.pdf |title=Pitt Basketball 2008–09 Media Guide, pg. 132, accessdate 03–04–09 |access-date=2009-03-05 |archive-date=2018-11-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181112084600/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/pitt/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/0809-mediaguide-section8.pdf |url-status=dead }} In 2001–02, Knight was named [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Conference co-Player of the Year]], [[Big East Conference|Big East]] [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player|Most Improved Player]], First Team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]], and was named to the All-[[Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] team. Knight achieved Second Team All-Big East honors in 2002–04. He was a two-time [[United States Basketball Writers Association|United States Basketball Writers Association (USBWA)]] All-Region selection (2001–02 and 2003–04) and a USBWA/[[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] All-District Team selection in 2001–02. He won the USBWA Region Player of the Year in 2001–02.{{Cite web |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/pitt/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/0809-mediaguide-section8.pdf |title=PItt Basketball 2008–09 Media Guide, pg. 133–134, accessdate 03–04–09 |access-date=2009-03-05 |archive-date=2018-11-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181112084600/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/pitt/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/0809-mediaguide-section8.pdf |url-status=dead }} Knight finished his career at Pitt holding the school records for career assists (785), career assist average (6.2 assists per game), career steals (298), season assists (251 in 2001–02), and season minutes played (1,284 in 2001–02). Knight's #20 jersey was retired by Pitt prior to the Marquette game on March 4, 2009.[http://pittsburghpanthers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030409aaa.html Brandin's Night: Pitt Retires Brandin Knight's No. 20 Jersey], PittsburghPanthers.com, March 4, 2009. Accessed March 4, 2009. == Professional career == He played professionally for two seasons with the [[Asheville Altitude]] of the [[NBDL]]. Knight signed a contract with the [[NBA]]'s [[Houston Rockets]], but suffered an injury two weeks later that effectively ended his playing career. === Post-playing career === Knight worked as Director of Basketball Operations for the Pittsburgh men's basketball team during the 2007–08 season and was promoted in June 2008 to an assistant coach following the departure of [[Orlando Antigua]] to the [[University of Memphis]]' coaching staff. On April 13, 2016, Knight was officially introduced as the new assistant head coach for Rutgers following eight seasons at Pittsburgh.{{cite web |title=Former Pitt assistant Brandin Knight joins staff at Rutgers |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/15232638/former-pitt-assistant-brandin-knight-joins-staff-rutgers |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 5, 2026 |date=April 19, 2016}} He signed a four-year extension with Rutgers in April 2024.{{cite news |last1=Thompson |first1=Stephen |title=Pitt Legend Signs Extension With Rutgers |url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/pitt-panthers-legend-brandin-knight-signs-extension-rutgers |access-date=April 5, 2026 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=April 19, 2024}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Knight, Brandin}} [[Category:1981 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:All-American college men's basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Asheville Altitude players]] [[Category:Houston Rockets players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Livingston, New Jersey]] [[Category:Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball coaches]] [[Category:Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball coaches]] [[Category:Seton Hall Preparatory School alumni]] [[Category:Sportspeople from East Orange, New Jersey]] [[Category:Basketball players from Essex County, New Jersey]] [[Category:Undrafted NBA players]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]]
